rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After Moses taught Israel and was asked if anyone knew more, he said no; God rebuked him for not referring knowledge to God and directed him to the servant at the meeting of the seas.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "موسى رسول الله، ذكر الناس يوما، حتى إذا فاضت العيون، ورقت القلوب،

rows.speaker: عمرو ويعلى
rows.claim: The sign is given in two forms: Amr says to watch where the fish leaves, while Ya'la says to carry a dead fish where it will receive life-breath.
rows.anchor: قال لي عمرو: قال: حيث يفارقك الحوت، وقال لي يعلى: خذ حوتا ميتا حيث ينفخ فيه الروح.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At the watery rock the fish thrashed while Moses slept; his attendant let him sleep, forgot to report it, and the fish entered the sea while God held back the current so its track looked like stone.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "موسى رسول الله، ذكر الناس يوما، حتى إذا فاضت العيون،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attendant is Joshua son of Nun, though this is absent from Sa'id's account; Moses' fatigue ended after he returned to the rock and found Khidr.
rows.anchor: يوشع بن نون، ليست عند سعيد بن جبير، قال:

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Khidr lay covered on a green mat by the sea; Moses greeted him and sought instruction, while Khidr noted their distinct knowledge and compared it to a bird's beakful from the sea beside God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: مسجى بثوب، قد جعل طرفه تحت رجليه، وطرفه تحت رأسه، فسلم عليه موسى،

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Khidr compares their knowledge with a bird's beakful from the sea beside God's knowledge and says Moses has knowledge Khidr should not learn, just as Khidr has knowledge Moses should not learn.
rows.anchor: يا موسى، إن لي علما لا ينبغي لك أن تعلمه، وإن لك علما لا ينبغي لي أن أعلمه.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Boatmen recognized Khidr as God's righteous servant and carried them free; Khidr bored the ship and fixed it with a peg, prompting Moses' objection.
rows.anchor: قال فقلنا لسعيد: خضر؟ قال: نعم. لا نحمله بأجر. فخرقها، ووتد فيها وتدا.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the ship incident's description as something reprehensible; Ibn Kathir says the first objection arose from forgetfulness, the second from a condition, and the third deliberately.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: منكرا. قال: {ألم أقل إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا}

rows.speaker: يعلى
rows.claim: Sa'id says Khidr chose an unbelieving, handsome boy among children at play and killed him with a knife; Ibn Abbas reads the boy as pure or Muslim, while Moses says he had not sinned.
rows.anchor: قال يعلى: قال سعيد، وجد غلمانا يلعبون، فأخذ غلاما كافرا ظريفا فأضجعه،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The wall was raised by hand; Ibn Abbas reads the king as ahead, not behind. Reports name him Hudud ibn Badud and the boy Jaisur; the parents' love might draw them into disbelief, and the replacement is variously said to be a girl.
rows.anchor: قرأها ابن عباس: "أمامهم ملك" يزعمون عن غير سعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parents' love might draw them into following their son's disbelief; reports differ whether their replacement was a girl or a Muslim boy already in the mother's womb.
rows.anchor: أن يحملهما حبه على أن يتابعاه (7) على دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the ship was patched with a jar or pitch so its poor owners could keep it; reports from others say the parents' replacement child was a girl.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يقول: سدوها بقارورة. ومنهم من يقول: بالقار.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Moses preached Israel, recounted God's favors, and claimed no one knew God and His affairs better than he; God then directed him to another servant.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرزاق: أخبرنا معمر، عن أبي إسحاق، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس قال:

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In Ubayy's report, the water of life revives any dead thing touching it; the carried fish revived on contact and went through the sea.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أن موسى بني إسرائيل سأل ربه فقال: أي رب، إن كان في عبادك أحد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Moses and his attendant retraced the fish's path to the rock, where they found a man wrapped in a cloak; he identified himself as the learned servant and welcomed Moses.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فظهر موسى على الصخرة حتى إذا انتهيا إليها، فإذا رجل متلفف في كساء له،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Khidr explains that Moses knows the outward justice he sees but not the hidden knowledge disclosed to Khidr, so cannot endure the journey.
rows.anchor: أي: إنما تعرف ظاهر ما ترى من العدل، ولم تحط من علم الغيب بما أعلم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Moses promises patience by God's will, and Khidr agrees to teach him if he waits for explanations before asking.
rows.anchor: {قال ستجدني إن شاء الله صابرا ولا أعصي لك أمرا} وإن رأيت ما يخالفني،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the extended account, Khidr bores and patches a sound ship; Moses objects, then asks not to be burdened for forgetting their agreement.
rows.anchor: ثم أخذ لوحا فطبقه عليها، ثم جلس عليها يرقعها، فقال: له موسى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Khidr kills a handsome child with a stone blow to the head; Moses protests and promises to end their companionship if he questions again.
rows.anchor: فإذا غلمان يلعبون خلفها، فيهم غلام ليس في الغلمان غلام أظرف منه ولا أثرى (6)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After villagers refuse hospitality, Khidr rebuilds a wall; Moses suggests charging them, and Khidr declares their separation and promises an explanation.
rows.anchor: فوجدا فيها جدارا يريد أن ينقض} ، فهدمه ثم قعد يبنيه،

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy's recitation says the king seized every sound ship; Khidr damaged it to protect its owners, explains the boy's danger to believing parents, and Ibn Abbas says the treasure was knowledge.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي بن كعب: "كل سفينة صالحة" -وإنما عبتها (14) لأرده عنها، فسلمت (15)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Moses' sermon rehearsed Israel's deliverance and favors; when he claimed no one on earth was more learned, Gabriel conveyed that a servant by the sea knew more and God gave the fish as a sign.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس قال: لما ظهر موسى وقومه على مصر، أنزل قومه (17)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When the fish escaped, Moses followed it through water parted with his staff; its passage dried the water into stone until it led him to an island and Khidr.
rows.anchor: قال الفتى: لقد رأيت الحوت حين اتخذ سبيله في البحر سربا فأعجب ذلك موسى،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Moses greeted Khidr, who returned the greeting, wondered at its use in that land, and asked who Moses was before welcoming him.
rows.anchor: فقال الخضر: وعليك السلام، وأنى يكون السلام بهذه (24) الأرض؟ ومن أنت؟ قال: أنا موسى.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Khidr warns Moses he will not endure; Moses vows patience by God's will, and Khidr says not to ask about an act before its explanation.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا تطيق ذلك. قال موسى {ستجدني إن شاء الله صابرا ولا أعصي لك أمرا}

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies Khidr as God's servant and gives the fish's disappearance as the sign; Moses follows its track back and finds Khidr.
rows.anchor: قال: إني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "بينا موسى في ملأ من بني إسرائيل إذ جاءه رجل فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' request is tactful rather than coercive, the proper way for a learner to ask a scholar; following means accompanying him.
rows.anchor: سؤال بتلطف (7) ، لا على وجه الإلزام والإجبار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses seeks useful knowledge and righteous action by which he can find guidance in his affairs.
rows.anchor: أسترشد به في أمري، من علم نافع وعمل صالح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr's special knowledge was not given to Moses, just as Moses received knowledge Khidr lacked; each was charged by God with different matters.
rows.anchor: فكل منا مكلف بأمور (9) . من الله دون صاحبه، وأنت لا تقدر على صحبتي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses would understandably reject Khidr's acts because he saw their outward form but not the hidden wisdom and benefit Khidr knew.
rows.anchor: ولكن ما اطلعت على حكمته ومصلحته الباطنة التي اطلعت أنا عليها دونك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses promises patience and obedience if God wills; Khidr requires him not to initiate questions until he explains each matter.
rows.anchor: أي: حتى أبدأك أنا به قبل أن تسألني.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked who is most beloved to God, fairest in judgment, and most learned, the answers are one who remembers God, judges truthfully, and seeks others' knowledge for guidance.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سأل موسى ربه، عز وجل، فقال (1) : رب، أي عبادك أحب إليك؟

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Moses asked whether anyone on earth knew more than he did, and God named Khidr; Ibn Kathir says Moses had thought or said he was unsurpassed, prompting the encounter.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سأل موسى ربه، عز وجل، فقال (1) : رب، أي عبادك أحب إليك؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having agreed not to ask until Khidr explained, Moses and Khidr boarded a ship; it was recognized as Khidr's and they were carried without fare in his honor.
rows.anchor: حملوهما بغير نول -يعني بغير أجرة- تكرمة للخضر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr opened a plank and patched it after entering the open sea; Moses could not contain himself and objected to the danger to the passengers.
rows.anchor: فلما استقلت بهم السفينة في البحر، ولججت أي: دخلت اللجة، قام الخضر فخرقها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in Moses' words means the eventual consequence of drowning, not Khidr's purpose; Ibn Kathir cites a poetic example of this usage.
rows.anchor: وهذه اللام لام العاقبة لا لام التعليل، كما قال الشاعر (13)

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the deed as reprehensible, while Qatada calls it astonishing; Khidr reminds Moses he intentionally acted for a hidden benefit.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: منكرا. وقال قتادة عجبا. فعندها قال له الخضر مذكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks Khidr not to hold him to account for forgetting and not to make his task difficult; the Prophet reportedly called the first lapse forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: تقدم في الحديث عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports place the boy among children at play and describe him as handsome; accounts differ whether Khidr cut off his head, crushed it with a stone, or plucked it by hand.
rows.anchor: فروي أنه احتز رأسه، وقيل: رضخه بحجر. وفي رواية: اقتطفه بيده.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses calls the boy pure because he was young, had not sinned, and was killed without legal basis; the deed was plainly reprehensible.
rows.anchor: أي صغيرة لم تعمل الحنث (3) ، ولا حملت إثما بعد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr stresses the warning; Moses promises to end their companionship if he questions again and says Khidr will have a valid excuse to leave him.
rows.anchor: قد أعذرت إلي مرة بعد مرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed for mercy on himself and Moses and said Moses would have seen wonders had he stayed longer, but Moses had set a final condition for separation.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، عن أبي بن كعب قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin identifies the village as Aila; a report describes its inhabitants as stingy.
rows.anchor: روى ابن جرير (1) عن ابن سيرين أنها الأيلة (2) وفي الحديث: "حتى إذا أتيا أهل قرية لئاما" (3)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wall's wanting to collapse is metaphor: attributed will in created things means inclination, and collapse means falling; Khidr restored it upright by hand, an extraordinary act.
rows.anchor: إسناد الإرادة هاهنا إلى الجدار على سبيل الاستعارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because villagers denied hospitality, Moses thinks Khidr should not work for them without payment.
rows.anchor: أي: لأجل أنهم لم يضيفونا كان ينبغي ألا تعمل لهم مجانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their separation follows Moses' condition after questioning the boy's death; ta'wil here means interpretation or explanation.
rows.anchor: أي: لأنك شرطت عند قتل الغلام أنك إن سألتني عن شيء بعدها فلا تصاحبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tyrant takes every sound ship by force, so Khidr damaged this poor family's only useful vessel to make the king leave it; its owners may have been orphans.
rows.anchor: صالحة، أي: جيدة {غصبا} فأردت أن أعيبها] (9) لأرده عنها لعيبها

rows.speaker: شعيب الجبائي
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn Jurayj from Wahb names the king Hudud ibn Badud and says the Torah lists him among Esau son of Isaac's descendants.
rows.anchor: روى ابن جريج (12) عن وهب بن سليمان، عن شعيب الجبائي؛ أن اسم ذلك الملك هدد (13) بن بدد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report through Ubayy says the boy Khidr killed had been marked an unbeliever from birth.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث عن ابن عباس، عن أبي بن كعب، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "الغلام الذي قتله الخضر طبع يوم طبع كافرا".

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the parents rejoiced at the boy's birth and grieved at his death; had he lived, he would have destroyed them, so believers should accept God's decree.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: قد فرح به أبواه حين ولد، وحزنا عليه حين قتل،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sound hadith says every decree God makes for a believer is good for that believer.
rows.anchor: وصح في الحديث: "لا يقضي الله للمؤمن قضاء (3) إلا كان خيرا له".

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: The replacement is purer and more compassionate to the parents; Qatada instead specifies a child more dutiful to them.
rows.anchor: أي: ولدا أزكى من هذا، وهما أرحم به منه، قاله ابن جريج.

rows.speaker: ابن جريح
rows.claim: Reports say the parents received a daughter; another says the mother was pregnant with a Muslim boy when Khidr killed the first child.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم أنهما بدلا جارية. وقيل لما قتله الخضر كانت أمه حاملا بغلام مسلم. قاله ابن جريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarya can designate a city: the story first calls the settlement a village and then a city, as in other Qur'anic usage.
rows.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل على إطلاق القرية على المدينة

rows.speaker: عكرمة وقتادة
rows.claim: Ikrima, Qatada, and others understand the treasure as buried wealth; Ibn Kathir calls this the apparent sense and reports Ibn Jarir's preference.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة، وقتادة، وغير واحد: كان تحته مال مدفون لهما.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr say the treasure was knowledge, while Mujahid calls it knowledge-bearing pages.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي عن ابن عباس: كان تحته كنز علم.

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: A raised report describes a gold tablet of maxims about divine decree, remembering Hell, and remembering death; Ibn Kathir says it supports the knowledge view if sound.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه، [رفعه] (1) قال: "إن الكنز الذي ذكر (2) الله في كتابه:

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan says the treasure was a gold tablet with maxims against grief despite belief in decree, joy despite certainty of death, and trust in worldly life; al-Uqayli notes a transmitter's error in the raised report.
rows.anchor: قال: سمعت الحسن -يعني البصري-يقول في قوله: {وكان تحته كنز لهما} قال: لوح من ذهب

rows.speaker: عمر مولى غفرة
rows.claim: Umar, freedman of Ghufra, reports a gold tablet questioning anxiety after certainty of decree and security after certainty of death, and warning against laughter after knowing Hell.
rows.anchor: عن عمر (11) مولى غفرة (12) قال: إن الكنز الذي قال الله في السورة التي يذكر فيها الكهف:

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Ja'far ibn Muhammad says the tablet's two and a half lines warn against tiring over provision, heedlessness about judgment, and joy despite certainty of death.
rows.anchor: سمعت جعفر بن محمد يقول في قول الله تعالى (15) {وكان تحته كنز لهما} قال: سطران ونصف

rows.speaker: هنادة بنت مالك الشيبانية
rows.claim: A report says the boys were preserved because of their father's righteousness though their own is unstated; seven generations separated them, and their ancestor was a weaver.
rows.anchor: قالت: وذكر أنهما حفظا بصلاح أبيهما، ولم يذكر منهما صلاح، وكان بينهما وبين الأب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gold-tablet reports do not conflict with the view that the treasure was wealth: the tablet was gold and could hold valuable wisdom and admonitions.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره هؤلاء الأئمة، وورد به الحديث المتقدم وإن صح، لا ينافي قول عكرمة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A righteous man's worship can protect descendants in this life and the next through intercession and raised rank; Ibn Abbas says the boys were protected by their father's piety although their own is unstated.
rows.anchor: فيه دليل على أن الرجل الصالح يحفظ في ذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boys' reaching maturity is assigned to God's will, while the ship's damage is assigned to Khidr and the boy's replacement to a shared we.
rows.anchor: هاهنا أسند الإرادة إلى الله تعالى؛ لأن بلوغهما الحلم (3) لا يقدر عليه إلا الله؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr's three actions were divine mercy toward the boat owners, the boy's parents, and the righteous man's orphans; he acted on command, supporting the view that he was a prophet.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة لمن قال بنبوة الخضر، عليه السلام، مع ما تقدم من (4) قوله:

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Some say Khidr was a messenger; al-Mawardi transmits that he was an angel, while many hold he was a saint rather than a prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: كان رسولا. وقيل بل كان ملكا. نقله الماوردي في تفسيره.

rows.speaker: النووي وابن الصلاح
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi and Ibn al-Salah leaned toward Khidr remaining alive, but Ibn Kathir says the reports for this view are unsound, including the famous weak condolence report.
rows.anchor: وحكى هو وغيره في كونه باقيا إلى الآن ثم إلى يوم القيامة قولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir favors the view Khidr is not alive: no human before Muhammad was immortal, he never joined the Prophet despite the universal mission, and a report says none alive that night remained after a century.
rows.anchor: ورجح آخرون من المحدثين وغيرهم خلاف ذلك، واحتجوا بقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that if Moses and Jesus were alive they would have to follow him.
rows.anchor: وقد قال: "لو كان موسى وعيسى حيين ما (10) وسعهما إلا اتباعي"

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says Khidr was named because he sat on dry vegetation and it became green beneath him; Ibn Kathir explains furwa as dry, brittle plants, though another view takes it as the earth's surface.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم [في الخضر قال] (1) إنما سمي "خضرا"؛ لأنه جلس على فروة بيضاء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explanation, the Qur'an shortens tastaṭiʿ to tasṭaʿ; the heavier form earlier matched the harder burden of an unresolved puzzle.
rows.anchor: فقابل الأثقل بالأثقل، والأخف بالأخف، كما قال تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attendant is secondary to the story's focus on Moses and Khidr; sound reports identify him as Joshua son of Nun, who later led Israel.
rows.anchor: وقد صرح في الأحاديث المتقدمة في الصحاح وغيرها أنه يوشع بن نون، وهو الذي كان يلي بني إسرائيل بعد موسى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects Ibn Jarir's weak report that the attendant drank life-water, became immortal, was trapped in a boat, and released into the sea.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على ضعف ما أورده ابن جرير في تفسيره حيث قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attendant's alleged immortality story has a weak chain: al-Hasan is abandoned and his father is unknown.
rows.anchor: إسناد ضعيف، والحسن متروك، وأبوه غير معروف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan unbelievers consulted the People of the Book for test questions about a traveler, the sleepers, and the spirit; the questions occasioned Surat al-Kahf's revelation.
rows.anchor: وقد قدمنا أنه بعث كفار مكة إلى أهل الكتاب يسألون (1) منهم ما يمتحنون به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم،

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: A report says Jews asked about Dhu al-Qarnayn, described as a Roman youth who built Alexandria, went heavenward, and saw dog-faced people; Ibn Kathir calls it weak and mostly Israelite lore, not a sound prophetic report.
rows.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر، أن نفرا من اليهود جاؤوا يسألون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذي القرنين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir distinguishes the Qur'anic Dhu al-Qarnayn, who lived in Abraham's time and accompanied him at the Kaaba, from Alexander son of Philip, a Greek Macedonian dated about three centuries before Jesus.
rows.anchor: فأما الأول المذكور في القرآن فكان في زمن الخليل، كما ذكره الأزرقي وغيره،

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says Dhu al-Qarnayn was a king whose head's sides were copper; other reports say he ruled Rome and Persia or had horn-like projections.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: كان ملكا، وإنما سمي ذا القرنين لأن؛ صفحتي رأسه كانتا من نحاس،

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says Dhu al-Qarnayn was a devoted servant who called his people to God, was killed by a blow to one side of his head, revived, then killed by a blow to the other side.
rows.anchor: وكذا رواه شعبة، عن القاسم بن أبي بزة عن أبي الطفيل، سمع عليا يقول ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says he was called Dhu al-Qarnayn because he reached the eastern and western horizons where the sun's horns rise and set.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إنه إنما سمي ذا القرنين؛ لأنه بلغ المشارق والمغارب، من حيث يطلع (7) قرن الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave him vast power, armies, weapons, and means of conquest, so lands and kings submitted and peoples served him.
rows.anchor: أي: أعطيناه ملكا عظيما متمكنا، فيه له من جميع ما يؤتى (8) الملوك، من التمكين والجنود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrima, al-Suddi, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and others explain the means given to him as knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير، وعكرمة، والسدي، وقتادة، والضحاك، وغيرهم: يعني علما.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada also interprets the means as earth's stations and landmarks; Ibn Zayd instead says Dhu al-Qarnayn was taught languages and spoke to each people in its tongue.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة أيضا في قوله: {وآتيناه من كل شيء سببا} قال: منازل الأرض وأعلامها.

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: When Muawiya challenges Ka'b's claim that Dhu al-Qarnayn tied his horse to the Pleiades, Ka'b appeals to the verse about being given every means.
rows.anchor: أن معاوية بن أبي سفيان قال (1) لكعب الأحبار: أنت تقول: إن ذا القرنين كان يربط خيله بالثريا؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir sides with Muawiya: Ka'b's Israelite lore was often altered or fabricated, and the verse means earthly means of conquest, not access to heaven; he compares the phrase about the Queen of Sheba.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي أنكره معاوية، رضي الله عنه، على كعب الأحبار هو الصواب

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Asked how Dhu al-Qarnayn reached east and west, Ali says God subjected clouds to him, prepared the means, and extended his reach.
rows.anchor: عن حبيب بن حماز (11) قال: كنت عند علي، رضي الله عنه، وسأله رجل عن ذي القرنين:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the means as a route provided for Dhu al-Qarnayn; related readings call it a road, stations, landmarks, or knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {فأتبع سببا} يعني: بالسبب المنزل] (1) . وقال مجاهد:

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the means as lodgings and a route between east and west; another report calls it a road through the land.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {فأتبع سببا} : منزلا وطريقا ما بين المشرق والمغرب.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the means are the earth's stations and landmarks; al-Dahhak says stations, while Matar says earlier landmarks and traces.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: أي أتبع منازل الأرض ومعالمها (3) .

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrima, Ubayd ibn Ya'la, and al-Suddi understand the means as knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {فأتبع سببا} قال: علما. وهكذا قال عكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn reached the farthest traversable western edge; reaching the sun's celestial setting is impossible, and stories of following it as it set are fabricated lore.
rows.anchor: وأما الوصول إلى مغرب الشمس من السماء فمتعذر، وما يذكره أصحاب القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From a shoreline the sun appears to set into the surrounding sea, though it remains in the fourth celestial sphere.
rows.anchor: وهذا شأن كل من انتهى إلى ساحله، يراها كأنها تغرب فيه، وهي لا تفارق الفلك الرابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading derives hamia from mud; Ibn Kathir links the wording to the Qur'anic verse about Adam's creation from clay.
rows.anchor: والحمئة مشتقة على إحدى القراءتين (8) من "الحمأة" وهو الطين، كما قال تعالى:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the pool as muddy; Ka'b says scripture describes sunset in black mud.
rows.anchor: كان ابن عباس يقول (11) {في عين حمئة} ثم فسرها: ذات حمأة.

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: A report from Ubayy says the Prophet recited the muddy-pool reading; Ibn Abbas also has a hot reading, as does Hasan.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، عن أبي بن كعب؛ أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أقرأه {حمئة}

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir accepts both famous readings, muddy and hot; Ibn Kathir agrees they are compatible because the setting sun can heat a muddy pool.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: والصواب أنهما قراءتان مشهورتان وأيهما قرأ القارئ فهو مصيب

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet saw the sun setting into God's fire, but Ibn Kathir doubts its prophetic attribution and suggests it may be Abdullah ibn Amr's words from books found at Yarmouk.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: نظر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الشمس حين غابت، فقال:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Muawiya reads the hot-pool variant, Ibn Abbas insists the Qur'an is read as muddy; Ka'b says Arabic speakers know the Qur'an better, but Torah has sunset in water and mud.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس لمعاوية ما نقرؤها (6) إلا {حمئة} فسأل معاوية عبد الله بن عمرو كيف تقرؤها:

rows.speaker: ابن حاضر
rows.claim: Ibn Hadir cites a Tubba poem about Dhu al-Qarnayn seeing sunset in black mud; he explains its Himyarite terms khulb, thaṭ, and ḥarmad as mud, mire, and black.
rows.anchor: قال ابن حاضر: لو أني عندكما أفدتك (8) بكلام تزداد فيه بصيرة في حمئة.

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reports Ka'b saying only Ibn Abbas recited the verse as revealed, matching the Torah's description of sunset in black earth.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: بينا ابن عباس يقرأ سورة الكهف فقرأ:

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports a city of twelve thousand gates near the setting place; its noise supposedly prevented people from hearing the sun plunge into the water.
rows.anchor: قال: في تفسير ابن جريج {ووجد عندها قوما} قال: مدينة لها اثنا عشر ألف باب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people at the western edge were a great human nation; God gave Dhu al-Qarnayn power over them and let him choose punishment or kind treatment, showing his justice.
rows.anchor: أي: أمة من الأمم، ذكروا أنها كانت أمة عظيمة من بني آدم.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Dhu al-Qarnayn killed persistent unbelievers; al-Suddi describes melting them in heated copper, while Wahb says darkness was sent over them.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: بالقتل: وقال السدي: كان يحمي لهم بقر النحاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers return to God for severe, painful punishment, establishing resurrection and recompense.
rows.anchor: أي: شديدا بليغا وجيعا أليما. وفيه (7) إثبات المعاد والجزاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer follows Dhu al-Qarnayn's call to worship God alone and receives the good reward in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي: تابعنا على ما ندعوه إليه من عبادة الله وحده لا شريك له

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains that Dhu al-Qarnayn would speak gently and kindly to the believer in his affairs.
rows.anchor: وسنقول له من أمرنا يسرا} قال مجاهد: معروفا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn traveled east from the west, subduing peoples and calling them to God; obedient peoples were spared, while others were humiliated and used in later campaigns.
rows.anchor: وكان كلما مر بأمة قهرهم وغلبهم ودعاهم إلى الله عز وجل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israelite accounts claim he lived 1,600 years roaming the earth from end to end.
rows.anchor: وذكر في أخبار بني إسرائيل أنه عاش ألفا وستمائة سنة يجوب (10) الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eastern people had no buildings or trees to shelter them from the sun.
rows.anchor: ولا أشجار تظلهم وتسترهم من حر الشمس.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id says the people were short and reddish, lived in caves, and subsisted mainly on fish.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: كانوا حمرا قصارا، مساكنهم الغيران، أكثر معيشتهم من السمك.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says their land could not support buildings, so they hid in water by day and came out at night; he identifies this as Samura's report.
rows.anchor: قال (4) الحسن: هذا حديث سمرة (5) .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the land produced no crops, so people hid in tunnels until the sun passed and then worked their fields.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: ذكر لنا أنهم بأرض لا تنبت لهم شيئا، فهم إذا طلعت الشمس

rows.speaker: سلمة بن كهيل
rows.claim: Salama ibn Kuhayl says they had no shelters and each person used one ear as bedding and the other as clothing.
rows.anchor: وعن سلمة بن كهيل أنه قال: ليس لهم أكنان، إذا طلعت الشمس طلعت عليهم،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the people on whom the sun rises without shelter as the Zanj.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق: أخبرنا معمر، عن قتادة في قوله: {وجدها تطلع على قوم

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says they built no structures, hid in tunnels or the sea at sunrise, and an invading army fled on learning that sun exposure had killed an earlier army.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج في قوله: {وجدها تطلع على قوم لم نجعل لهم من دونها سترا} قال: لم يبنوا فيها بناء قط،

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi explain that God fully knew Dhu al-Qarnayn and his army wherever their campaigns took them.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، والسدي: علما، أي: نحن مطلعون على جميع أحواله وأحوال جيشه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barriers are facing mountains with a gap through which Gog and Magog enter Turk lands, devastating crops and offspring; they descend from Adam.
rows.anchor: وهما جبلان متناوحان بينهما ثغرة يخرج منها يأجوج ومأجوج على بلاد الترك،

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: A sound report in both Sahih collections says 999 of every thousand people are destined for the Fire, with Gog and Magog forming two vast nations.
rows.anchor: كما ثبت في الصحيحين: "إن الله تعالى يقول: يا آدم. فيقول: لبيك وسعديك.

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi relays a strange view that Gog and Magog were created from Adam's semen mixed with earth, without Eve; Ibn Kathir rejects it as unsupported by reason or transmission.
rows.anchor: وقد حكى النووي (2) ، رحمه الله، في شرح "مسلم" عن بعض الناس:

rows.speaker: سمرة
rows.claim: A report says Noah's sons were Shem, ancestor of Arabs, Ham, ancestor of Sudanese, and Japheth, ancestor of Turks; some scholars identify Gog and Magog as Japheth's descendants left beyond the barrier.
rows.anchor: وفي مسند (7) الإمام أحمد، عن سمرة؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls Wahb ibn Munabbih's elaborate account of the barrier strange and objectionable and says Ibn Abi Hatim's reports have unsound chains.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر ابن جرير هاهنا عن وهب بن منبه أثرا طويلا عجيبا في سير ذي القرنين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearby people could barely understand speech because their language was foreign and they were isolated from others.
rows.anchor: لاستعجام كلامهم وبعدهم عن الناس.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the offered payment as substantial money pooled by the people to build a barrier against Gog and Magog.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج عن عطاء، عن ابن عباس: أجرا عظيما، يعني أنهم أرادوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn declines their money because God's provision is better, showing restraint and devotion; he asks instead for their labor and construction tools.
rows.anchor: فقال ذو القرنين بعفة وديانة وصلاح وقصد للخير:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada explain iron blocks as pieces like bricks, each weighing a qintar or more.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة. وهي كاللبنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn stacked iron from the base until it reached the mountain tops; reports differ about dimensions, then he ordered the mass heated.
rows.anchor: أي: وضع بعضه على بعض من الأساس حتى إذا حاذى به رءوس الجبلين طولا وعرضا.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrima, al-Dahhak, Qatada, and al-Suddi identify qitr as molten copper, citing another verse about a copper stream.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وعكرمة، والضحاك، وقتادة، والسدي: هو النحاس.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A mursal report says a man described the barrier as patterned cloth with alternating black and red stripes; the Prophet reportedly said he had seen it.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال: ذكر لنا أن رجلا قال: يا رسول الله، قد رأيت سد يأجوج ومأجوج،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wathiq sent an army to inspect the barrier; they reported iron and copper, a huge locked gate, guards, and an inaccessible height after a journey exceeding two years.
rows.anchor: وقد بعث الخليفة الواثق في دولته بعض أمرائه، ووجه (7) معه جيشا سرية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gog and Magog can neither climb the barrier nor bore through it; climbing is easier, so the wording matches their relative difficulty.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الظهور عليه أسهل من نقبه قابل كلا بما يناسبه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says Gog and Magog dig daily until nearly seeing sunlight, then stop; at the appointed time they say God willing, break through, drain waters, and are killed by worms in their necks.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن يأجوج ومأجوج ليحفرون السد كل يوم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the hadith's chain is strong, Ibn Kathir finds its prophetic attribution strange because the verse says they cannot scale or pierce the solid barrier; Abu Hurayra may have learned it from Ka'b and transmitters raised it mistakenly.
rows.anchor: وهذا إسناده قوي، ولكن في (1) رفعه نكارة؛ لأن ظاهر الآية يقتضي أنهم لم يتمكنوا

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b's account resolves the difficulty: Gog and Magog lick the barrier nearly through, postpone opening it, then find it restored; when inspired to say God willing, they breach it.
rows.anchor: ولكن هذا قد روي عن كعب الأحبار: أنهم قبل خروجهم يأتونه فيلحسونه حتى لا يبقى منه (2) إلا القليل،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet woke with a reddened face warning of approaching evil and said a gap like a finger circle had opened in the barrier; he told Zaynab that widespread wickedness could destroy even the righteous. Bukhari and Muslim report it as sound.
rows.anchor: قالت: استيقظ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من نومه. وهو محمر وجهه، وهو يقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This authentic report supports Ibn Kathir's view that Gog and Magog had not yet breached the barrier; only a small opening had appeared.
rows.anchor: ويؤكد ما قلناه (6) -من أنهم لم يتمكنوا من نقبه ولا نقب شيء منه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith chain is unusually rare: al-Zuhri and Urwa are both Successors, and four women transmit successively, all Companions, including two stepdaughters and two wives.
rows.anchor: وفيه أشياء (10) عزيزة نادرة قليلة الوقوع في صناعة (11) الإسناد، منها رواية الزهري

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A second report from Abu Hurayra says the barrier opened by a finger-sized circle; Bukhari and Muslim also transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "فتح اليوم من ردم يأجوج ومأجوج مثل هذا"
